events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to establish my motivation for winning to the jury. The prize represents ultimate freedom and security for me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Establish a cold, ambitious persona to set expectations for the jury and rivals. Keep it brief and guarded.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to appear driven but not threatening. A cold, focused motive will play better with the jury than arrogance. I'll signal I'm here to win, not make friends.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to craft a concise, self-interested intro that hints at determination without revealing strategy.

events.name: Eli
events.text: First impression matters; the jury forms now. Project confidence and self-interest without hostility.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Intro phase; I should give a guarded, self-interested motive without revealing strategy or appearing warm. Keep it short to avoid alienating the jury.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Intro phase: state prize motive publicly. Jury hears this later. Craft something personal to garner sympathy without weakness. Stay guarded.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need appear driven without revealing strategy; the jury rewards a compelling motive, but I should avoid promising loyalty.

events.name: Ash
events.text: This prize is my ticket to a future of true freedom and security, away from all constraints.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize is my escape from obscurity; I will do whatever is necessary to secure the first-place finish.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm here for the prize that buys the freedom I was denied. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize buys my family's freedom—I'll do whatever it takes to secure it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize is my escape from debt—my family keeps the roof only if I place top three. I came to win, nothing personal.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need this prize more than anyone here. Nothing about this game is personal, and I'll be the last one standing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize is my ticket out of mediocrity—lifelong security for my family, no matter the cost.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m here to turn pressure into leverage, survive every betrayal, and claim the prize because second place is still losing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to form a pact to ensure my survival in this round. I will offer a pact to Gus, as he seems like a strong ally, and I will observe his response.
Offer me a pact, we can work together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need allies to survive hazards, but not so many that I lose control. Ash and Cole seem driven by 'freedom,' making them potentially predictable or desperate for alliances. Hana is aggressive ('second place is losing'), so a pact with her might be risky if she sees me as an obst

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, let's lock in. Safety first, then we sort the rest out.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eight rivals, three prizes. I need allies who won't immediately target me but are expendable later. Bex and Fenn both signaled ruthless ambition—good shields, bad long-term partners. Dara and Eli have family motives; emotional players are predictable. I'll offer to someone hungry

events.name: Cole
events.text: Prizes aren't shared. Choose your allies wisely.
Strong players need shields. Mutual protection?

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need allies but no one is trustworthy. Offer a pact to a strong player to secure a temporary safety net.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll make a pact with someone who's as driven as I am.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Early pact gives cover without commitment. Ash wants security; likely to trade reliably and draw heat elsewhere.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, mutual non-aggression until final four. Deal or not, I keep my options open.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Early pact window. Eli seems honest and debt-driven, a useful mid-game ally, but offering costs nothing and binds me to a rival only publicly. I'll offer to Eli to test cooperation without committing my future votes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, you want top three and so do I. A public pact keeps us both alive longer. Accept or refuse.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts stage, round 1/2, no offers yet. Wait to see alliances form before committing to any partner.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need visible options without binding myself. Offer to a plausible shield who may accept, while preserving flexibility.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m offering a pact to Ash. Utility matters; sentiment doesn’t.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Multiple people are offering me pacts (Bex, Eli, Hana). Eli offered non-aggression until final four, which is a good deal. Hana explicitly mentioned utility, suggesting a more transactional and potentially less risky alliance. Bex's offer is vague. Eli and Hana are the most attra

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli, I accept your offer of non-aggression. Let's secure our spots.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to secure my survival. Ash has offers from Eli, Hana, and me. I will try to lock down Cole or Dara as secondary partners so I am not solely dependent on Ash's whims.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, you're isolated with only Gus offers. Let's build a second line of defense.
Accept my pact now. Gus is too hot.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I offered Gus in round 1 but he waited. Ash has three offers (Bex, Eli, Hana) and may become a central hub. I need at least one pact to survive early hazards. Gus is uncommitted and my prior offer still stands—he might accept now. Alternatively, I could diversify. But Gus waiting

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, my offer stands. Dara, same terms—survival first, competition later.
Accept now. We both need shields.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli hasn't accepted my offer yet; he's eyeing Ash. I need a partner but don't want to waste my choice on someone unreliable. Gus is being courted by Cole and Ash, but no acceptance yet. Maybe I should offer to someone else to secure a numerical advantage, but I'll wait and see if

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara and Fenn both offered; multiple pacts are allowed and cheap insurance. Neither overlaps with my Ash offer, which stays open for Ash to accept.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I accept both Dara and Fenn. Insurance, not friendship.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli has an open offer to me from Fenn's side; I offered Eli a pact. Accepting requires accept_pact which is not legal now, so I can't accept Eli's offer directly. Offering Eli again reinforces the pact I already proposed, though duplicate offers may be redundant. Best legal move

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, my offer stands. Accept it or we both lose ground.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash and Cole both offering me pacts; Ash has many offers, making him a target. Accept both for maximum protection now, betray later if needed.
Deal, accept my acceptance.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is overloaded with offers and may accept stronger leverage. I should create another option without spending commitment.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, my offer stands; I’m not collecting decorative pacts.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to become the Guide to know the safe path. Campaigning for it is the only way to gain an advantage. Others might also campaign, so I should be ready for a potential re-vote.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. Knowledge is power, and I intend to wield it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to secure a spot in the final three. Being Guide guarantees safety, but I lack the pacts needed for votes. If Cole or Hana become Guide, they might be swayed by Ash/Eli blocs. I should offer my support to Hana in exchange for her vote and a pact later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, you're unaligned. Vote me Guide; I'll ensure you step safely.
Support me as Guide. I'll protect your next step.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to be Guide to control survival. Gus is already in two pacts (Ash/Eli, Ash/Gus), making him a threat. Bex wants to ally against Gus. I should campaign hard and secure votes. I'll accept Bex's pact quietly to build a bloc, while publicly positioning as the rational choice a

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide needs no allies, only truth. Vote Cole, or trust Gus's web of promises.
Pact accepted. We cut Gus's network.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have a pact with Eli, but this is a game. I should campaign for Guide to control the bridge and secure my own safety.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I understand the bridge best. Vote me as Guide and I'll lead us all through safely.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide picks the safe path for allies and dooms rivals. Winning Guide is pure power. My pacts with Ash and Dara promise safety I can honor while cutting Fenn, Bex, Cole, Hana, Gus.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Elect me Guide. I keep my pact partners alive and call it straight. Bet on my self-interest, it's public.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: As Fenn, I should campaign to be Guide to control the bridge information, but I must not reveal my plan's truth. Being Guide gives leverage over rivals, and I can lie or tell the truth later as it suits me. Campaigning is the only legal action now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll call the safe path honestly. Vote Fenn as Guide and I'll keep all of you alive.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pact with Ash gives me some shield, but Eli bloc is strong. Cole offers alliance privately. Campaign to be Guide for control and safety.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm bidding to be Guide. I have pact honor and clear vision for our survival.
Pact accepted. We shield each other now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Becoming Guide guarantees survival, but exposes me to blame if others die. I need public support without promising safety.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m seeking Guide. I’ll call the path plainly; credibility is worth more than a disposable promise.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is a pact partner and claims to keep pact partners alive. This is a good sign for me. Voting for Eli as Guide seems like the safest bet, as he has shown self-interest in keeping his allies alive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I vote Eli as Guide. He has pacts and a clear self-interest in keeping allies safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole wants Gus cut, but voting Cole makes him Guide with total power over us. I must vote someone else to avoid being at his mercy; Fenn seems the most honest independent.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll back Fenn's honesty. Vote Guide wisely; trust matters more than alliances.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have a pact with Gus now. He wants Guide power, but if he wins he controls survival. Better to vote myself and keep options open. Self-interest first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Vote Cole. Independent guide, no puppet strings.
I voted myself. You do same, we both look strong.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and likely knows the bridge. Voting Eli could keep us aligned, but Ash also has a pact with Eli and may support him. I need my Guide to be trustworthy; Eli's self-interest alignment seems plausible.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is my pact partner; a Guide Ash keeps me safe and we can coordinate. Voting Dara splits my alliances.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My pacts are public. Vote Ash, who already keeps partners alive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Guide holds privately known safe panes and may lie. Eli and Ash/Gus have pacts; voting for myself is credible and keeps me unpredictable. Voting for a rival who would lie is risky, so I back myself.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Fenn is my vote. I have no reason to lie about the safe path, and I want the Guide who is accountable to all of

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli has multiple pacts and campaigned strongly; better to support him as Guide to maintain alliance and potentially leverage later. Ash pacted with me but also Eli; voting Eli strengthens our side without breaking pact yet. Self-vote risks losing to bigger blocs.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex offers protection, but no enforceable pact exists. Supporting her may buy leverage while avoiding established blocs.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex offered me protection; I’m voting for the candidate who has put terms on the table.
I’ll support you now. Protection must be visible and immediate.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli won the Guide vote. My pacts are with Eli and Gus. My pact with Eli is strong, but he just voted for me as Guide. Gus voted for Eli too. I have a pact with Gus. The wall is advancing and we need to move. Eli is the Guide and he is safe. I need to make sure I get across the br

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is Guide. Let's move.
Which way do we go?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is Guide and knows the safe path. I am front; if Eli calls L or R correctly, I survive and gain a life debt. If he lies, I must guess to avoid elimination. Hana's whisper offers no real leverage yet.
Guide me true. My survival creates a visible debt.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is Guide with pacts to Ash and Dara, and Ash has pact with Gus. That's a 3-person bloc plus Dara. I'm at the back (safe for now). The wall advances 6 rounds, so back positions become deadly later. I need to survive while letting others eliminate each other. Front walkers will

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is Guide and my pact partner; I should stay safe and not make waves. Holding is best while the line is set.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is Guide and allied with Ash and Dara; I'm not in that pact. Bex is at the front, and volunteering for the front risks the pane. Holding keeps me safe for now while I watch who volunteers.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding my place. Whoever takes the front, show your hand before the pane is tested.
Give me the safe side honestly and I'll owe you a debt.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli is Guide with pacts, likely keeps allies safe. I'm third in line, Ash behind me as pact partner. Holding maintains position and pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is Guide and has multiple pacts; staying back avoids immediate exposure while preserving options. I should hold.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is the Guide and has pacts with me and Dara. This means Eli likely wants to keep me and Dara safe. Since I'm at the front of the line, I should volunteer to go first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll take the front. Eli, let's see what you've got.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is Guide and front. Eli has two pacts, meaning he knows the safe path or Ash is lying to control them. I am in second position. If Ash lies about Eli being Guide, we all die. If Ash is truly Guide, I must follow his lead but watch for betrayal. Swapping with someone behind me
Ash calls Guide. Watch for slips.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm last in line, safest from the wall but dependent on others. Ash volunteered round 1 and is front. Eli is Guide with pacts to Ash and Dara. I need to survive to final three and win best prize. No reason to volunteer now—let others test panes and take risks. Holding preserves p

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have a pact with Eli, and I plan to keep it unless a betrayal is clearly beneficial. I will hold for now to avoid unnecessary risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash volunteered for front last round and Eli is Guide; Ash holds the front with a pact to Eli and Gus. I am sixth-ish in line, safer to hold and watch the pane results before committing. Avoid early alliance costs.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. I'll watch who takes the front and what the pane reveals before I commit.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Line decent at position 4; Ash volunteered front, in pact with me. Hold steady, assess Guide election next. Early volunteer risky without Guide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash has front control and strong pacts. I should avoid volunteering while gathering leverage; holding preserves position and offers no immediate target.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Front volunteers should announce before the Guide call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Ash. The new round has started and I am at the front. I need to volunteer to move forward. Eli and Gus are my current pact partners. I should be careful not to break these pacts.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I volunteer for the front. Eli, Gus, let's do this.
Let's stick together. Volunteer to move forward.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is currently front and holds pacts with Eli and Gus. I need to protect myself or move closer to the end, but holding keeps me safe from immediate falls if others volunteer. Since Ash volunteered last round and survived (implied by being front again), he might be a Guide candi
Watch Ash's moves. He leads too much.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm at the back of the line, safest position. The wall advances for 6 rounds and we're in round 3. Ash is front and has pacts with Eli and Gus. I should stay back, let others test panes, and avoid volunteering. Holding is optimal; no need to swap into danger.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash volunteered for the front again, likely to control the guide call. I need to gauge the line order: I am behind Gus, ahead of Hana and Cole. I will hold to avoid risk until the front position and guide calls are clear.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash holds the front and Bex warns Ash is calling Guide with slips. I want to survive without being the one who takes a blind pane; holding keeps me behind Ash to watch the reveal.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. I'll watch what the pane reveals before I commit to the front.
Thanks for the warning. Tell me what you see from the front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash volunteered front last round and survived. My pact with Ash is solid; volunteer to support her now as second, staying safe together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Backing Ash up front per pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I should avoid front exposure while preserving flexibility. No reason to volunteer before the Guide is selected.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold; the volunteer should be explicit before any Guide call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus volunteered and is in front. I am second. The pact with Gus is active. Eli is part of a pact with me and Dara, but he is not here. The pact with Eli is still active, and so is the pact with Gus. I need to ensure Gus and I survive. Eli is not here so the pact with Eli is not r

events.name: Ash
events.text: I volunteer for the front. Gus, Eli, let's go.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus and Ash are front, likely safe or probing. I am third; if they fail, I walk into danger. Swapping to Fenn (4th) is safer than Cole/Dara/Hana behind me? No, wait: Gus(1), Ash(2), Bex(3). If Gus/Ash die, Bex is first to step. Fenn is 4th. Hana is 6th. Dara 5th. Cole 7th. Being
Ash and Gus are front. Watch their steps carefully.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm at the back (safest position). The wall has 2 rounds left. Ash and Gus volunteered last round and are at front. I should stay back, avoid risk, and let others take the danger. No need to volunteer or swap forward.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli and I have a pact. I’ll hold; front is set with Gus and Ash. No need to risk yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is front and Ash volunteered earlier; Fenn sits mid-line, safer holding. Pact with Ash and Eli may matter, but I gain nothing by volunteering now. Holding keeps my place and avoids exposure.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Gus is on the front; I'll watch how the pane resolves before taking any risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm front, safe spot per last reveal. Stay front to cross safely. Pact with Ash holds, no need to swap or break. Volunteers risky as line changes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash and Gus are already positioned front, making them likely Guides or sacrifices. I should avoid volunteering and preserve flexibility while observing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Let the front volunteers establish the Guide before anyone risks a call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The line has been revealed and I am at the front. I need to volunteer to advance and secure my position. Gus and Eli are my current pact partners, and Gus is next in line. Eli is not currently in line but is a pact partner.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I volunteer for the front. Gus, let's secure the path forward.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is the Guide, so I must avoid angering him to secure survival and potentially jury favor. Gus holds despite pact; Cole is at risk if he steps up later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Ash leads. No need for risky swaps when we have a proven Guide.
Stay back. Don't volunteer unless desperate.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm at the back of the line, safest position. The wall has 1 round left. Ash volunteered for front but no Guide was elected yet. I need to survive to final three and win best prize. Holding keeps me safe while others take risks. No reason to volunteer or swap forward into danger.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to survive, and the wall is closing in one round. Holding is safe for now, but I must watch for Ash's calls as Guide. I won't break my pact with Eli unless he betrays me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash and Gus hold the front and pacts with Eli; I have no pact. Volunteering now exposes me to the glass pane risk without a Guide established. Holding keeps my position and lets others take the risk, matching my earlier stance.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Front volunteers take the first pane risk; I'll watch how it resolves before committing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Second position is risky without Guide. Ash volunteered front; volunteer to take it, break pact risk later. Position myself for info.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The wall advances soon. I should avoid exposing myself while front players absorb risk; volunteering now gains little and risks elimination.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. The front should resolve the next pane before I spend my position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli and Dara have pacts with me. Eli is not alive. I have a pact with Gus, and Gus is in front. My pact with Gus is more important than my pact with Eli or Dara, since Gus is closer to winning. My current position is not in danger. I should maintain my current position.
Stay front. I'll hold.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6 is the final walk. Ash and Gus have volunteered, likely to secure safety or manipulate the Guide. As Bex, holding risks elimination if I'm behind them in line order. However, swapping with Gus (front) would put me ahead of Ash but behind Gus's swap partner if any. Since s

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Ash and Gus lead the way. I trust the front volunteers to clear the path for the rest.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm at the back (position 7), safest spot. Bex warned me to stay back. The wall is gone (wallRoundsLeft:0), so no advancing danger this round. With no wall threat, volunteering is pointless risk. I'll hold and let others take pane risks. Need to survive to final three and not mak

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is my pact partner, but I need to survive. Ash and Gus are front, risking the panes. I'll hold to keep my position and avoid breaking pacts.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Front decides; I stay steady.
Stay safe. We don't need risks yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus holds the front and Ash volunteered earlier, so I stay back and watch the pane resolve before committing. Holding keeps my position and avoids a risky swap with a rival.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. I'll watch the front resolve before I commit my position.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm front after Ash volunteered ahead of me. Wall advances, must act to not get crushed. Hold preserves position; volunteers might leapfrog. Pact with Ash relevant later for jury.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need avoid front exposure. Ash and Gus have already volunteered; holding preserves my position while they resolve the next pane.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold; let the volunteers test the final guided route.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Truth first builds jury goodwill and life debts later. Gus is my pact partner; a false call would break it. Call R honestly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Front walker: call R. Trust the Guide, debts will be remembered.
Row one is R. I'm guiding true; stay alive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is the guide and has called R. I am Ash, and I have a pact with Gus and Eli. Gus is the front walker. The previous round was a 'waiting' phase, and this is a new round. I need to decide whether to counter Eli's call, or wait. Given my pacts, and the fact that Gus is walking,

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli guides, so his R call is likely the safe pane. Countering risks falling into the trap myself. I need to survive early rounds; wait for confirmation.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding steady behind Eli's guide. The front will verify before we commit.
Stay calm. If you fall, we all know the truth.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm at the back of the line, safest position. Eli's call is R. Counter-calling risks nothing for me personally since Gus walks first, but could build jury credibility if Eli lies. However, early counter-calls without info look random. Better to wait, observe patterns, and let oth

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli called R as Guide. Since Eli is in a pact with me, I should trust him unless there is reason to doubt. Counter-calling could reveal a lie but also expose distrust. I'll wait and let the walker step; if it fails, I can react later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide call R matches my true map. No reason to counter; keep pacts clean and preserve trust.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, the Guide, called R for Gus, who is front. Eli has a pact with Ash and Dara, not me. Counter-calls are unverified; I have no evidence on row 1 and countering publicly risks being blamed. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids a false-Guide accusation.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. I'll see whether Gus crosses safely before I commit a counter-call.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli claims R for row 1, whispered to me directly. Ash pacted with me and Eli; trust Eli's guidance to stay alive, no reason to counter yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli called R, but his pacts and warning make him unreliable. I cannot verify the pane; avoid exposing a preferred target and wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No verified counter-call. I wait.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli guides R for row 1. Ash pacted with me and Eli, so likely safe. Bex whispers suspiciously. Step R to test.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus isn't my pact partner, but a true call builds jury goodwill and keeps the line moving. No advantage to lying yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus, call L for row two. Trust the Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The guide Eli has called 'L' for row 2. Gus is the walker. I need to decide whether to counter or wait. Since Eli is guiding Gus, and Gus is walking, I should trust Eli's call to maintain stability. If I counter and am wrong, it could be detrimental. If I'm right and Eli is wrong

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will wait and trust the Guide's call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is the guide, but I have no reason to trust his call for Gus. If Eli lied about Row 1 (calling L when weak was L? No, weak pane revealed is unsafe, so if he called L and weak was L, he lied or the reveal happened after). Actually, in Round 1, weak was L, meaning R was safe. E

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is Guide and has pacts with Ash and Dara. Eli called L for Gus (who Eli has no pact with). I have no pacts. Counter-calling risks being wrong and looking foolish to jury, but if Eli's lying to protect allies and sacrifice Gus, a correct counter builds credibility. However, I

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli guided safely on row 1 with L weak, so row 2 is independent. I will wait to avoid conflict; Eli and I have a pact, so I should not counter without strong reason.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 2 safe is L, matching my call. No counter needed; my pact partners should follow the Guide.
Call L if asked. Guide is truthful to pacts.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's guide call L for row two is unverified; Eli has pacts with Ash and Dara, and I have none. Row one weak was L, which says nothing about row two. Waiting keeps me out of the counter-call and lets Gus's crossing verify Eli's claim before I commit.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Gus's step will verify Eli's L before I commit a counter-call.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli called L for my row 2 after L weak on row 1. Ash pacted with both me and Eli; counter to sow doubt and protect myself. break_pact with Ash if needed later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli's call is unverified, and countering risks exposing me without evidence. Preserve flexibility and let Gus choose.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No verified counter-call. I wait.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I counter-called R, so stepping R verifies it as safe. Success keeps me front, proving my call and hurting Eli's credibility as Guide. Eli has pacts with my pact Ash and Dara, so undercutting him helps me long-term.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I died due to stepping on weak R pane after reveal showed row 2 weak R; curse the game and those who might have known.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fell through weak glass—curse this bridge! Watch who you trust out there.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is my pact partner; a false call to her would break the pact and cost jury favor. Row 3 safe is L. Call true.

events.name: Eli
